A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of Legal Retrieval for Public Defenders. Text and visual comparison cover the main paper, references, and all appendices. Differences are confined to first-page author and version information.

before.justification: v1 reports original BriefBank evaluations, retrieval-model experiments, and reranker results in Section 5, Table 2, and appendix Tables A4-A8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original retrieval, fine-tuning, and reranker results, including the detailed appendix outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain the same retrieval/reranking pipeline, synthetic-data generation and filtering, IRAC query expansion, and legal domain adaptation. No components, objectives, or procedures change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NJ OPD and public PD datasets, BarExam-QA, LePaRD, synthetic training corpora, and US case-law domain-adaptation data. No tasks or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eight pretrained retrieval models and fine-tuned e5-large-v2 row. The ModernBERT comparisons and reranker comparator sets, including the majority baseline, are identical in Tables A7-A8.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same whole-dataset retrieval evaluation, metrics, model configurations, and 80/20 query-separated reranker split. Reported preprocessing and training settings also match.

E4.justification: The query-category error analyses, training-data and query-expansion comparisons, cross-dataset correlations, and alternative-metric checks remain unchanged in Sections 4-5 and the appendices.

E5.justification: Both report five independent fine-tuning runs with different seeds, 95% confidence intervals, and identical significance and correlation reporting, including Tables A5 and A7.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains 37.37% PD Recall@5 for Qwen3-Embedding-8B, and Table A8 retains 88.4% held-out F1 for the fine-tuned reranker.

T1.justification: Section 2.3's query-to-paragraph retrieval definition is identical. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and no mathematical reasoning is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about public-defense retrieval, benchmark mismatch, and benefits from domain knowledge, curated synthetic data, and query expansion.

C2.justification: Interpretations of domain mismatch, NV-Embed evaluation bias, failures on nuanced or keyword queries, and limitations of generative tools remain unchanged in Sections 2 and 4-6.

D1.justification: Data-processing instructions, training hyperparameters, annotation guidelines, and generation/query-expansion prompts are identical. The embedded code and dataset access links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 42 references, related-work discussion in Section 6.4, and positioning against existing legal-retrieval datasets in Table A1 are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Inyoung Cheong to the author list and updates the arXiv stamp from v1 dated 20 January 2026 to v2 dated 24 February 2026. Scientific prose and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: The added author slightly changes line wrapping in the first-page byline. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged; pages 2-24 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates authorship and version information while retaining the same methods, evidence, claims, reproducibility details, and appendices. The slight byline reflow produces no meaningful change in readability or overall scientific quality.
